summary: Covers YAML booleans (use lowercase true/false for yamllint), multi-line values with literal `|` (keeps newlines) and folded `>` (newlines become spaces), keeping specific newlines with blank lines, extra indentation, or `\n`, and a combined example.
questions: How do I write a multi-line string in YAML?
What's the difference between | and > in YAML?
Should I write true or True or yes for booleans?
How do I keep some line breaks in a folded > block?

answer_card.title: YAML booleans and multi-line strings
answer_card.answer_md:
Booleans can be written several ways (`true`, `True`, `TRUE`), but use lowercase `true`/`false` to stay compatible with default yamllint options.

Multi-line values (indentation is ignored):
```yaml
include_newlines: |
  exactly as you see
  will appear these three
  lines of poetry

fold_newlines: >
  this is really a
  single line of text
```
- `|` (literal block scalar) keeps newlines and trailing spaces.
- `>` (folded block scalar) folds newlines to spaces.

In a `>` block, a blank line or extra indentation keeps a newline, or write `\n` explicitly in a quoted string: `"a b\nc d\n  e\nf\n"`.
